$comment: The takeoff review visual law. ONE declaration, two consumers: apps/web/src/takeoff/partition-review.tsx (the partition review on the web) and eval/rhvac/render-zone-promotion.py (the offline agent-review renderer). Neither may hold a colour or a layer rule the other cannot see. Before this file existed the two surfaces had already diverged: /runs deleted the invented-closure dither at feedback round 2 ('read as confusion, not honesty') and the python renderer kept drawing it, so the human and the delegated eyes were judging different claims.
laws: The VERDICT render draws only what the solver claims exists, over what is actually there. Nothing invented. No input layer except the zone outline.
Decisions, evidence, and inputs never share a hue family.
Status is never carried by the candidate boundary. The candidate fill edge IS the boundary.
Received ink is the only near-opaque neutral. Invented closure is a translucent warm tint, never dithered, never screened.
The plan is what is there. The ink raster is what the solver saw. Judge against what is there; adjudicate against what it saw.

plan.$comment: 6000px Revit export with an exact affine (topLeft/topRight/bottomLeft in model feet). The export is halftone-light: measured, 1.44% of pixels sit at or below 185 and that band is the whole linework. Stretch it.
plan.$resampleAmendment: v1.3 2026-08-23. ORDER MATTERS AND v1.2 IMPLIED THE WRONG ONE. Measured on Lower Level (the worst case at 11.4 px/ft, where a 4in interior wall spans 3.8 px across BOTH faces): stretching at native resolution and then reducing to a card viewport destroys thin walls - they break into dashes and the regular ones moire. Reducing with a filtered resample FIRST and stretching after keeps them continuous. kaitpw flagged this on 3 of 6 cards ('moire sort of pattern', 'internal walls look like dashed lines', 'really really poor exported plan quality') and it was the renderer, not the export.

resample.$comment: Any reduction to a target viewport uses an area/Lanczos filter and happens BEFORE the tone stretch. Applies to card viewports, contact sheets, and A/B pairings alike. Plan-native (1:1) renders skip the reduction and may stretch directly.

plan.$pointsComment: Tuned for POST-reduction tone. Filtered averaging lightens thin lines, so the pre-reduction 185/235 over-darkens and clips. At 1:1 with no reduction, 185/235 remains correct.

ink.$comment: replay seed ink, 0.5ft cells. EVIDENCE, not substrate. Forensic render only.

fill.$amendment: v1.1 2026-08-23. v1 said 'saturated' and 'fillDarkened' without numbers, so each consumer would have invented its own and the two surfaces would have drifted on day one. These are the values lane W shipped; they are now the law.
fill.$comment: Saturated translucent, stable across runs so an A/B keeps its colours. Adjacent candidates must differ enough that the seam between two fills reads as a boundary at 1px.

zone.$comment: kaitpw ruling 2026-08-23: zone authority stays visible in the verdict render, but hairline. It is an input, not a result, and it may never be the heaviest stroke in the image. Ruling 2026-08-28: this law owns the semantic dashRole; base.css owns the only numeric pattern. Both consumers resolve --dash-<role> there, so a raw dash array may never come back here.

invented.$comment: Sealers manufacture obstruction. Forensic render only, translucent warm tint, never dithered.

$washAmendment: v1.2 2026-08-23. v1 was WRONG: voidWash and excludedWash both composited to RGB 226 over white and were indistinguishable (found by lane R implementing them faithfully). Worse, kaitpw's first annotation pass flagged excluded residue in 4 of 4 zones - it is the top-ranked defect class - so it must be the more legible of the two, never a near-invisible wash. Void stays a neutral grey; excluded becomes a warm tint that a 1 ft sliver still shows.
$residueAmendment: v1.3 2026-08-23. A solid wash cannot serve both jobs. Excluded residue is the top-flagged defect class and its instances are THIN (1 ft ribbons along wall bands), but a single instance can also be HUGE - Lower Level#03 is 2,579 sf of one excluded blob, and rendered as a solid it hid 85% of the zone's plan. kaitpw: 'the opaque excluded residue blocks the view of plan ... very bad but I'm not sure why' - unable to diagnose because the render painted over the evidence. Outline guarantees a 1 ft sliver registers; hatch keeps a 2,500 sf blob transparent. NEITHER MAY EVER OBSCURE THE PLAN.

label.$comment: Status letter + candidate id. Small, on the fill, never on the boundary.
